pr_title: Improve legacy hitcircle texture lookup to match 1:1 with stable
pr_body:
- Closes #17869 

On stable, in the case of a slider head piece (same applies to slider tail): 
 - if `sliderstartcircle` exists but `sliderstartcircleoverlay` doesn't, then nothing is displayed.
 - if `sliderstartcircle` doesn't exist but `sliderstartcircleoverlay` does, then the overlay is ignored and `hitcircle` + `hitcircleoverlay` is used instead.

On master, the first bullet is satisfied by not looking up with `hitcircle` subsequently if `sliderstartcircle` exists, but the second is not (resulting in #17869).

I've simplified things so that there's no "fallback" logic, and the first lookup with `priorityLookup` decides whether subsequent lookups should be done with either `priorityLookup` or `hitcircle`, without falling back between.

| before | after |
|--------|-------|
| ![CleanShot 2022-04-19 at 04 57 26@2x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/163920571-3cef8ca4-ba51-4baa-a791-58506baaa69f.png) | ![CleanShot 2022-04-19 at 04 55 56@2x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/163920534-51556eb9-dfeb-42ca-a3ca-db8d88279774.png) |

Test coverage included to ensure this doesn't potentially regress in the future.

issue_context.title: sliderstartcircleoverlay added when no sliderstartcircle is used
issue_context.body:
### Type

Cosmetic

### Bug description

Stable only shows the sliderstartcircleoverlay.png of a skin when there is also a sliderstartcircle.png but lazer always shows the overlay. This results in some legacy skins looking different on stable and lazer.
[Varv.osk.zip](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/8506372/Varv.osk.zip) (.osk file is inside the zip)

review_comments: Not sure if it is just me but I was really confused as to why an interface-typed mock is apparently delegating anything to base. (The answer is default interface implementations.)
Yeah, and the reason why this line exists in the first place is also because default interface implementation.
Have attached a comment to avoid confusion.

Where's this `canBeNull: true` spec coming from? The dependency was not previously allowed to be null.

Is it because of the pre-existing null check in `Dispose()` triggering a "never null" inspection or something?
More like because it’s used in a test scene in isolation, therefore needs to not require the DHO as a dependency.

I would have gone the other way and cached one for the sake of it but I'm not sure I care enough to argue this further? Like it seems weird to me that integral dependencies are being marked nullable just for the sake of a test, but alas.
I dunno, what's the proposed "better way" here? Prtobably just leave nullable for now.

Tying into the comment above, I believe that this has no right to occur in any real non-broken usage. I'd argue that it's better to let this loudly crash rather than silently not work, and therefore there should be a hard cast somewhere to non-nullable to elide all of the nullchecks.
